Measured 71.4M vs band max 60M on the dev solve arm — out of band for the first time (58.5M after W12 §1, inside it). The routed water enters every cell's water access downstream of any runoff and a month the land waters — the floodplain, the river, the lake, the routed stream — now counts toward a crop's season, so the static farmed capacity is higher wherever the land is watered (the density ordering's river cells 17.8 → 20.5 persons/km², its rainfed cells 9.8 → 11.6) and the same saturating curve, with no famine variance or mortality, reaches a higher ceiling sooner. The ceiling is M3b's (missing-mortality physics, population:-5000:dev); W13 raised it by wetting the land where the water is, which is the mechanism and not a rate. Recorded, not dialed. At dev P18 is inert by construction — the orographic footprint is zero at 240 wide, where a table cell is smaller than a map cell (third cardinal rule) — so every move on this arm is the paddy's alone: rice's fit rises on flooded ground in the flood months and every other package's falls there by its drowning loss, and nothing else in the grade changed. The river cells of the density ordering read 20.5 → 20.3 persons/km² (the drowning loss on the packages that hold the floodplains, where rice is not yet present), the rain-fed cells 11.6 → 11.6. The same curve against the same ceiling.

Measured 1.438 km/yr Balkans → Rhine on the dev solve arm against the band's 1.3 (Pinhasi, Fort & Ammerman 2005, 0.6–1.3); 1.420 after W12 §1, 1.077 before it. The corrected hop share is not a tuning: a hop of mean square ⟨d²⟩ delivers s·⟨d²⟩/4 of diffusivity, so the share that delivers D is 4·D·dt/⟨d²⟩ and not D·dt/area. The SAME constants measured 0.670 km/yr at the shipped grid after §1 — inside the band for the first time. Identical physics, two grids: the 167 km reference lattice moves a share of a whole cell's people 167 km in a single hop, so its pulled front outruns the continuum 2·√(r·D) the constants name, where the 42 km shipped lattice does not. W13 adds 0.018 km/yr at dev (a wetter Danube corridor carries a slightly denser front). A dev-raster row measured against the grid that ships (third cardinal rule); recorded, not dialed. Re-measured 2026-09-05 after W14 (P18 and the paddy): 1.420 km/yr — the Balkans one stride earlier and the Rhine one later; P18 is inert at dev (zero footprint at 240 wide) and the paddy does not touch wheat's months.

Measured −3106 vs latest −5000 (−4200 with the grace) on the dev solve arm — LATE, where every other reached row is early or on time. −3148 after W12 §1, whose corrected share is what first moved it; W13 (the routed water and the watered month) advanced it 42 years and no more, although the Luxor cell's wheat capacity at full technique rises 0.91 → 3.11 persons/km² at the shipped grid under W13 (the valley's winter now counts toward wheat's season, 5 → 8 months). The valley is farmed by sorghum from the Sudan, not by Levantine wheat (see staple:nile:solve:dev), so it is the sorghum route down the valley that sets the date, and sorghum's own belt lights at −6095. WHY a larger share should delay this one arrival is not isolated. The standing candidate is dilution: a firing moves about 2.3× the pre-§1 share out of each cell, and along a corridor one or two cells wide flanked by desert the leading edge thins faster than it accumulates the density adoption needs — which would make the Nile the first place the anisotropic flux of W12 §4 is visible. Recorded as the open question it is, not dialed. Re-measured 2026-09-05 after W14 (P18 and the paddy): −3099, one 84-month stride later; the valley still farms sorghum (staple:nile:solve:dev), whose fit the paddy lowers by the drowning loss on the flooded strip in the flood months — the open question above stands, unchanged in kind.

Recorded, not dialed.
